title: Clinic (team) admin and membership
summary: Invitation acceptance (Phase 11.1c) and the clinic's Team page (Phase 11.2). References show the clinic as a card, one clear question, which email the invite was sent to and a confirmed state with one next step; then one list of people with their role, pending invitations kept apart with Send again and Withdraw, and an invite dialog that says what each role can do and how long the invitation lasts. The Verification page (Phase 11.4) says where the check stands in one sentence, shows the reason when a change is needed, and keeps the form next to it. References 14 to 24 (2026-11-21) prepare the slices still to build: choosing a plan priced per seat, the Billing page with seats in use, the moment a clinic reaches its seat limit, a list of every session across the clinic's experts, a schedule with experts side by side, and a sensitive setting that is confirmed and shows who turned it on.

references.pattern: Accept page: the workspace as a card, one question, two buttons
references.why: A quiet centred page: 'Almost there!', the workspace as a small card (logo, name, URL), 'Do you want to accept your invite to this workspace?' with the terms line under it, then 'Yes, take me there' (primary) and 'Not yet' (secondary). Footer with privacy, support and sign out.
references.apply: Name the clinic and show it as a card; ask one question; offer accept and a gentle 'Not now' (decline) of equal clarity; keep legal lines small under the question.
references.query: accept an invitation to join a team workspace

references.pattern: Join page that says which email the invitation was sent to
references.why: 'Join ASMobbin on Slack' as the headline, a line on what it is, who has already joined, then 'You're accepting an invitation sent to samlee@…' above the form, so the person knows which address the invite belongs to.
references.apply: Say which email the invitation was sent to; if the signed-in account is different, say so and offer to switch account.
references.query: accept an invitation to join a team workspace

references.pattern: Invitation card with sender, address and 'Not you?'
references.why: A single card: illustration, eyebrow 'You're invited', 'Join alexsmith's Workspace', 'This invitation was sent to j•••@gmail.com', one button, and 'Signed in as … Not you?' at the bottom.
references.apply: Mask the invited address, show who is signed in, and give 'Not you?' to switch.
references.query: accept an invitation to join a team workspace

references.pattern: Invited → joined, with the next step in the same card
references.why: 'You've been invited to join' with the team card (name, 'invited by Alex Smith'); after accepting, the same card shows a check, 'You joined Alex's Family with jdoe@…' and 'Visit Team'.
references.apply: After accepting, confirm in place with who and where, and give one button to the clinic dashboard.
references.query: accept an invitation to join a team workspace

references.pattern: One list of people: name, email, role pill, and one primary 'Invite member'
references.why: Settings > Team is a single list: initials, name, email, a role pill (Owner, Partner, Collaborator) and when each joined, with one green 'Invite Member' button and a quiet 'Invite sent.' toast after sending.
references.apply: One list of people with name, email and a role pill; one primary 'Invite someone'; confirm a sent invitation with a toast, not a banner.
references.query: team members settings page with members list, roles and pending invitations

references.pattern: Members page that opens with one line on what you can do, and marks you and pending invites
references.why: 'Members' with one sentence under it (manage members, set their access level, invite up to the seats on your plan), then rows with '(You)' beside the signed-in person and 'Invite pending' / 'Wait to resend' states on invited rows.
references.apply: Open with the headline and one line; mark the signed-in person as '(you)'; show an invitation's state in words on its row.
references.query: team members settings page with members list, roles and pending invitations

references.pattern: Pending invitations as their own block with a count and Cancel on each row
references.why: 'Pending Invites (1)' is a separate block from members: the address, a delivery status and row actions ('Cancel', 'Copy link').
references.apply: Keep invitations in their own block with a count in the heading; each row has Send again and Withdraw. Eleva does not offer 'copy link': the link is only ever emailed to the invited address.
references.query: team members settings page with members list, roles and pending invitations

references.pattern: Invite dialog: email, then a role with one line on what it can do
references.why: 'Invite team member' with two fields, Email address and Role; each role option carries one line on what it allows ('Full edit rights on all boards'), then Cancel and Invite.
references.apply: Two fields only (email, role); say in one line what the chosen role can do in the clinic, in the clinic's words, not permission names.
references.query: invite team member dialog with email and role selection

references.pattern: Invite dialog that says how long the invitation is valid
references.why: 'Invite Teammates' with the workspace logo, a line that says invitations 'will be valid for 14 days', an email field with the role beside it and one 'Send invite' button.
references.apply: Say in the dialog what the person receives and that the invitation is valid for 7 days; show the last valid day on the pending row.
references.query: invite team member dialog with email and role selection

references.pattern: One card that says where the check stands, in a full sentence
references.why: 'We are reviewing your details' as the card title, one sentence under it on what happens, and one way back to the dashboard. Nothing else competes with it.
references.apply: The Verification page leads with one card: the state as a sentence ('We are checking your details') and one line on what the clinic has to do, which is usually nothing.
references.query: business verification status page showing details under review and what happens next

references.pattern: When something is needed: what happened, then what to do now
references.why: The account status page answers 'What happened and what do I need to do now?' in two sentences, next to a status and a short progress list (submitted, in review, completed).
references.apply: When staff ask for a change, show their reason under 'What to change' and put the form right below it, already filled with what was sent.
references.query: business verification status page showing details under review and what happens next

references.pattern: 'No action is needed on your end' while someone else has the next step
references.why: 'We're reviewing your application' with a line that says no action is needed, and a small timeline with dates on the side.
references.apply: While Eleva checks, say plainly that the clinic does not need to do anything, and show what was sent and when.
references.query: business verification status page showing details under review and what happens next

references.pattern: One compact card on the home page while an approval step is open
references.why: 'Complete approval to take payments' sits at the top of the dashboard as a small card: an icon, one sentence that says what it unlocks and one button. It is there only while the step is open.
references.apply: On the clinic's Overview, show one card only when verification needs the clinic: what stands, one sentence, one button to Verification. Nothing when Eleva is checking or the clinic is verified.
references.query: business banking dashboard home with an action required notice to finish business verification

references.pattern: Two plans as two cards priced per seat, with a seat stepper and a running bill summary on the same screen
references.why: 'Choose a Plan' shows Standard and Business as two cards, each with its price 'Monthly / per Editor', under a yearly or monthly choice. Beside them an 'Add Editors' stepper and a 'Bill Summary' give the total per month and the date of the first charge, with one button: 'Continue to Billing Details'. A two-step line on top says where she is.
references.apply: Show the clinic's two plans as two cards with the price per clinician seat; let the admin set the number of seats and watch the monthly total and first charge date change before she continues to payment.
references.query: workspace plans page comparing two paid plans with price per member

references.pattern: Change summary before paying: plan, billing period and seats on the left, what is due today and at renewal on the right
references.why: 'Upgrade to Pro' is one dialog: the billing period with the price per user per month, a seats stepper, and on the right '3 seat x Pro', subtotal, tax, 'Total at renewal' and 'Adjustment due today'. A note says the card is not charged until the trial ends. One button: 'Confirm and upgrade'.
references.apply: Before the clinic subscribes or changes plan, show one summary: plan, seats times price, tax, what is charged today and what renews on which date, then one button that names the action.
references.query: choose a team plan screen with plans priced per seat

references.pattern: Billing page that leads with the plan, then seats used out of seats included as numbers with a bar
references.why: 'Billing' opens with the plan name, 'Monthly', '$69.00 per seat/month' and when the billing period starts, with 'Explore Plans' under it. A Usage block reads 'Seats: 2 used / 2 included' above a bar. Billing email, company name and payment method follow. A quiet strip on top says how many trial days are left.
references.apply: Lead the clinic's Billing page with the plan and the price per seat, then 'Seats: 4 in use of 5 included' in words and numbers, with the bar only as a helper. Billing details and payment method come after.
references.query: workspace billing settings page with current plan, seats used and invoices

references.pattern: Billing as labelled rows, each with its own action: subscription, seats, then invoices
references.why: 'Workspace plan details' is a list of rows. Subscription reads 'Standard. Renews on March 2nd, 2026.' with Manage billing, Cancel plan and Update plan beside it. Workspace members reads '1 seat in use' with a line on what to do at the seat limit and a Manage button. An Invoices table follows with date, status, amount and a link to each invoice.
references.apply: One row per fact with its action beside it: plan and renewal date with 'Change plan' and 'Manage billing'; seats in use with a link to the Team page; past invoices as a table with date, status in words, amount and a download. Keep one primary button on the page, not one per row.
references.query: workspace billing settings page with current plan, seats used and invoices

references.pattern: At the seat limit, the invite dialog says the limit and offers the upgrade in place
references.why: Pressing invite at the limit opens 'Invite member to SL Mobbin' with one sentence: 'You have reached the maximum number of members for your workspace (1). Upgrade your workspace to add more members.' Two buttons: Cancel and Upgrade.
references.apply: When a clinic admin invites past the plan's seats, say how many seats the plan has and that all are in use, then what the larger plan gives (how many seats, at what price per seat), with 'See plans' and 'Not now'. Navattic names the limit but not what upgrading gives; Eleva says both.
references.query: upgrade prompt when a team reaches its seat limit

references.pattern: All appointments in one table: date range and filters on top, team member as a column, status in words
references.why: 'Appointments' has one line on what the page is for, then a search field, a date range, a Filters button and a sort. Each row shows the reference, service, who created it, scheduled date, duration, team member, price and a status that reads 'Booked' or 'Cancelled'. Export sits top right.
references.apply: The clinic's Sessions list: one row per session with date and time, member, service, clinician and status in words. A date range and a clinician filter stay visible above the table, with an export for the clinic's own records.
references.query: appointments list for a clinic filtered by staff member and date

references.pattern: Filter panel that names each filter, counts the ones in use and ends with Clear and Apply
references.why: 'Booking List' opens a side panel of filters: session date and time, booking status, payment status, service name, staff member, client name and location. A group in use shows a count, the footer says '2 filters selected' with Clear and Apply, and the Filter button carries a badge.
references.apply: Keep clinician and date as the two filters that are always visible and put the rest (status, service, online or in person) in a panel like this. Always show how many filters are on and one way to clear them all.
references.query: appointments list for a clinic filtered by staff member and date

references.pattern: Day calendar with one column per practitioner, portrait and name on top
references.why: The day view gives each team member a column headed by a portrait and a name. Hours outside working time are shaded, a red line marks the current time, and a booking block shows time, client and service. The controls on top are Today, the date with arrows, 'Scheduled team' and a Day switch.
references.apply: The clinic schedule's day view: one column per clinician who works that day, non-working hours shaded, each session block with its time, member and service. Offer 'Working today' and 'All clinicians' as the first filter.
references.query: team calendar day view with staff members in side by side columns

references.pattern: Week view with people as rows and days as columns, for when columns per person no longer fit
references.why: 'Work calendar' lists employees down the left with their role and the days across the top, with today marked. Each cell holds a labelled block ('09:00 AM - 05:00 PM, Remote', 'Paid time off - 1 day'). One line under the title sums up the day ('No employees out of office today'); filters and a Week or Month switch sit above the grid.
references.apply: For the week, switch to one row per clinician and one column per day, each cell showing her hours and number of sessions. Every block carries a text label, never colour alone, and the page opens with one line that sums up today.
references.query: team calendar day view with staff members in side by side columns

references.pattern: A sensitive access setting that says what it grants, asks for an explicit tick and a duration, then has one button
references.why: 'Allow access to your space for remote support' says in two sentences who gets access and why, and that it can be removed at any time. A tick box states what the admin agrees to, a Duration field is set to 30 days, and the button reads 'Allow access'.
references.apply: Letting a clinic's clinicians read each other's session records is its own block, not a bare switch: say who will be able to read what, ask for a written reason and an explicit tick, and name the button after the action. No Mobbin result asked for a written reason; Eleva adds that field.
references.query: grant support access to the workspace setting with an expiry

references.pattern: Who turned it on and when, in one line under the setting's name
references.why: The Figma integration's Connection tab shows 'Added by Sam Lee on Dec 2, 2024' right under the name, with 'Remove for everyone' beside it. An 'Action required' box says what is missing and has one button.
references.apply: Once shared records is on, show 'Turned on by {name} on {date}' under the setting with the reason she gave, and 'Turn off' beside it. Link to the clinic's activity log for the full history.
references.query: integrations settings with a connection that expired and needs to be reconnected

judging_criteria: Does the page name the clinic and who invited her, and show which email the invitation was sent to? (Attio 11-team/01, Slack 11-team/02, hilos 11-team/03)
Is there one clear accept action and an equally clear way to decline or not now, with what happens next said in plain words? (Attio 11-team/01, Craft 11-team/04)
If the signed-in account does not match the invitation, does the page say so and offer to switch, instead of failing? (hilos 11-team/03, Slack 11-team/02)
Do expired, cancelled and already-used invitations each say what happened and what to do?
On the Team page, can a clinic admin see within 5 seconds who is in the clinic, each person's role and who has a published service, with one clear way to invite? (Bonsai 11-team/05, Attio 11-team/06)
Are pending invitations kept apart from people, each with its last valid day (or that it expired) and with Send again and Withdraw on the row? (Krea 11-team/07, Attio 11-team/06)

Does the invite dialog ask only for email and role, say in plain words what the role can do and how long the invitation is valid, and refuse a bad address or an existing member with a sentence that says what to do? (Productboard 11-team/08, Dub 11-team/09)

Before someone is removed, does the confirmation name the person and the clinic and say what happens to their access, their services and their account, and does a refusal (sessions still to run, the owner, yourself) say why and what to do first?
On the Verification page, can a clinic admin tell in one sentence where the check stands and whether anything is needed from them? (Airwallex 11-team/10, Mercury 11-team/12)
When Eleva asks for a change or cannot verify, does the page show the reason in Eleva's own words and put the form to send new details right below it, filled with what was sent? (Stripe 11-team/11)
Does the form ask only for the legal name and the tax number, say what Eleva does with them, and refuse a malformed number with a sentence that says what a valid one looks like?
When verification needs the clinic, does the Overview say so in one card with one action, and stay quiet when it does not? (Square 11-team/13)

Can a clinic admin compare the two plans side by side with the price per seat, set the number of seats and see the total and the first charge date before she pays? (Sketch 11-team/14, Attio 11-team/15)

Does the Billing page show the plan, seats in use out of seats included in words and numbers, the next invoice date and amount, past invoices and one clear way to change the plan? (Attio 11-team/16, Runway 11-team/17)
When the clinic is at its seat limit, does the prompt say what the limit is, that it is reached and what the larger plan gives, with one way to continue and one way to close? (Navattic 11-team/18)

Can a clinic admin see every clinician's sessions in one list and narrow it by clinician and by date, with the filters in use always visible and each status in words? (Fresha 11-team/19, Wix 11-team/20)
Does the schedule show several clinicians side by side for a day and as rows for a week, with non-working time marked and every block labelled in text? (Fresha 11-team/21, Workable 11-team/22)

Before shared session records are turned on, does the clinic admin read who will see what, give a written reason and confirm explicitly, and does the setting then show who turned it on and when? (Productboard 11-team/23, Height 11-team/24)
